Hiiii! ✨  That’s pretty neat—I had no idea this was in the work.

I have a couple questions/comments if that’s okay?
- Is the use of `<search>` limited to one per page, or can it be used multiple times? The document doesn’t appear to explicitly clarify this.
- In the case it can in fact be used several times on a page, how would a given occurrence be differentiated from another for assistive technologies (e.g. landmark listing)? 

I guess where I’m coming at is that if it is _not_ unique per page (unlike `<main>`), maybe it should be a sectioning element so that it can essentially be labelled? That’s generally what’s recommended for `<nav>` elements, where we’d encourage authors to label them properly so multiple navigations can be differentiated from one another.

Unless I’m missing something? :)

thanks for the comment, @KittyGiraudel.  There is definitely guidance that can be added to flesh that out some more.

to quickly answer your questions though:
1. this element is different than `<main>`, as there can be more than one per document - though as with any landmark that exposes a landmark role, they should be used with purpose.  Will draft up some guidance for this.
2. With native HTML alone, the `title` attribute would be used to name the element, as there is no other mechanism available at this time without using ARIA.

I do think the comparison with `<nav>` is worth digging into though. I guess you can have multiple of each per page, and the question is whether we want to encourage `<hN>` children inside of them.

IIUC, for both `<nav>` and `<search>`, per https://w3c.github.io/html-aam/#section-elements-and-grouping-content-elements-not-listed-elsewhere you can only use `title=""` or ARIA. Using a `<hN>` will not suffice to give an accessible name.

Not sure where that leaves us...

Alright, I've added the `

` tag closing, and updated the OP with a summary of the state of things. I've additionally filed for TAG review at https://github.com/w3ctag/design-reviews/issues/714 . My guess on the next roadblock will be writing web platform tests, since per https://github.com/web-platform-tests/wpt/issues/27868 any tests involving the parser are annoying. But, it'd still be ideal to get editor review of this PR, and maybe prepare the PRs discussed in https://github.com/w3c/html-aria/issues/371 and https://github.com/w3c/html-aam/issues/369, so that we can merge this as soon as those are ready.

**As the [implementer of this feature *without form functionality*]( https://github.com/Kaleidea/chromium/commits/search-element-div ) in Chromium, I am OPPOSING this specification** until proper user research and origin trial is conducted.

I have put an order of magnitude more [effort]( https://kaleidea.github.io/whatwg-search-proposal/ ) (about 2 months) than all other participants combined into progressing this feature towards an outcome that best meets the web developer community's needs. The current proposal does not meet that purpose.

An [appeal]( https://github.com/whatwg/html/issues/7594 ) was filed according to the [workstream policy]( https://whatwg.org/workstream-policy#appeals ). Due to violations of WHATWG procedures and policies, this specification cannot be merged until those issues are resolved.

@domenic
1. Please register this opposition appropriately in the description.
2. Please add the "do not merge" label.

This is expected to happen within hours. Please respect my opposition and do not attempt to ignore or censor it, as [it happened before]( https://github.com/whatwg/html/pull/7320#pullrequestreview-802253725 ). I appreciate your fairness.

A new element with the same capabilities as `
` is a non-starter. The security fallout from that will take decades at best to iron out. `` is an XSS sink, plus it is able to perform fetches that are more powerful compared to other elements (it can perform `POST` requests etc) and navigation. A new element that can be a `form` would complicate all of the features that interact with forms, and each of those have a potential to break web content. The HTML parser has special knowledge about forms (e.g. the form element pointer). Extending that to also apply to a new element seems bad (and I expect is not going to be accepted by API owners for browsers' HTML parsers, as this, in itself, is an XSS-risky change), but also not doing that is somewhat bad because then previously-working page with `form` might break when switching to `search`. Furthermore, making a new element that *sometimes* act as a `form` (based on the presence of the `action` attribute) is even worse. That would likely be a source of bugs for a long time, if the experience with elements like `object` is any indication. As for the stated motivation: > 1. a [popular developer request](https://kaleidea.github.io/whatwg-search-proposal/#requests-for-this-feature) `` or `` seems like it would satisfy the requests without complicating everything and introducing new XSS risk and web compat risk. > 2. the best practice as demonstrated by the [MDN example](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/Accessibility/ARIA/Roles/Search_role) and the [WAI-ARIA example](https://www.w3.org/TR/wai-aria-practices/examples/landmarks/search.html). Examples in MDN and APG isn't a compelling argument for how to shape a new feature in my opinion. They show how to use existing features. > 3. the common sense [mental model](https://search-element-html-spec.netlify.app/multipage/forms.html#the-search-element): “The search element represents a part of a document or application that contains a set of form controls or other content related to performing a search or filtering operation.” A set of form controls is a form. `

` and `

` can also represent a set of form controls. It doesn't follow that they should also be forms. From what I can tell, making a new element act like a `form` violates these HTML design principles: - https://www.w3.org/TR/html-design-principles/#support-existing-content (changes to legacy APIs, form submission model, the HTML parser, etc, can break existing content) - https://www.w3.org/TR/html-design-principles/#degrade-gracefully (in legacy UAs users won't be able to submit forms) - https://www.w3.org/TR/html-design-principles/#do-not-reinvent-the-wheel (`form` already exists) - https://www.w3.org/TR/html-design-principles/#solve-real-problems (changes to fit a stated mental model, but the same use cases are possible with the alternative smaller and less risky change) - https://www.w3.org/TR/html-design-principles/#secure-by-design (introduce new XSS risk without introducing new functionality) - https://www.w3.org/TR/html-design-principles/#avoid-needless-complexity (as explained above)
